'''Iker Casillas Fernández''' ({{IPA|es|ˈikeɾ kaˈsiʎas feɾˈnandeθ}}; born 20 May 1981) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] and currently works as a [[football commentator]]. Dubbed "'''''San Iker'''''" ("Saint Iker"), he is considered to be one of the greatest goalkeepers of all time.{{refn|group=nb|
*{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/news-and-comment/james-lawton-spanish-can-always-have-faith-in-miracle-saves-of-saint-iker-casillas-7897190.html|title=James Lawton: Spanish can always have faith in miracle saves of 'Saint' Iker Casillas|last=Lawton|first=James|work=[[The Independent]]|date=29 June 2012|access-date=21 October 2015}}
*{{cite web|url=http://www.givemesport.com/352480-top-five-greatest-goalkeepers-of-alltime|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150507233748/http://www.givemesport.com/352480-top-five-greatest-goalkeepers-of-alltime|url-status=dead|archive-date=7 May 2015|title=Top five: Greatest goalkeepers of all-time|website=GiveMeSport|date=7 May 2015|access-date=19 February 2020}}
*{{cite web|url=https://www.calciomercato.it/news/156356/Campioni-ai-Raggi-X-Iker-Casillas-il-capitano-perfetto.html|title=Campioni ai Raggi X: Iker Casillas, il capitano perfetto|trans-title=Champions X-rayed: Iker Casillas, the perfect captain|publisher=Calcio Mercato|language=it|date=7 May 2012|access-date=21 October 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150930155417/https://www.calciomercato.it/news/156356/Campioni-ai-Raggi-X-Iker-Casillas-il-capitano-perfetto.html|archive-date=30 September 2015}}

*{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1516455-25-greatest-goalkeepers-in-football-history|title=25 Greatest Goalkeepers in Football History|last=Morgan|first=Richard|website=Bleacher Report|access-date=19 February 2020}}
*{{cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/101-greatest-football-players-last-25-years-full-list|title=Ranked! The 101 greatest football players of the last 25 years: full list|edition=253|work=[[FourFourTwo]]|date=13 February 2018|access-date=22 December 2023}}
*{{Cite web|url=https://bestfootballplayersever.com/top-10-best-football-goalkeepers-ever.php|title=Best Goalkeepers Ever – Top 10 list of the Greatest Football Goalkeepers Ever|website=Best Football Playerr Ever|access-date=19 February 2020|archive-date=25 June 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140625100316/https://www.bestfootballplayersever.com/top-10-best-football-goalkeepers-ever.php|url-status=dead}}
*{{cite news|url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/lists/buffon-or-yashin-top-10-goalkeepers-of-all-time/1mb2d3jk5w285150ykl834v60v|title=Buffon, Schmeichel or Yashin? Top 10 goalkeepers of all time|website=Goal.com|access-date=19 February 2020}}
*{{cite web|date=21 May 2020|title=The Debate: Iker Casillas - the greatest goalkeeper|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/the-debate-iker-casillas-the-greatest-goalkeeper_sto7754834/story.shtml|access-date=4 August 2020|website=Eurosport}}
*{{Cite web|date=4 August 2020|title='The Greatest Ever' – Itumeleng Khune Lauds Casillas After Retirement|url=https://www.soccerladuma.co.za/fan-park/the-best-of-the-rest/the-greatest-ever-itumeleng-khune-lauds-casillas-after-retirement/682861|access-date=4 August 2020|website=Soccer Laduma}}
*{{cite news|title=The 10 best goalkeepers in Champions League history|url=https://www.foxsports.com/soccer/gallery/champions-league-best-goalkeepers-ever-neuer-buffon-cech-van-der-sar-casillas-031417|access-date=4 August 2020|website=FOX Sports}}}} He is known for his athleticism, quick reactions and outstanding shot-stopping ability. Having spent the majority of his career at [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], Casillas is one of the few players to achieve over [[List of footballers with the most official appearances|1,050 professional career matches]], and also holds the [[List of world association football records|record]] for the most clean sheets for the [[Spain men's national football team|Spain national team]]. Currently, he works for [[RTVE]], [[Movistar Plus+]] and [[Azteca Deportes]].

At club level, Casillas started his career with the [[Real Madrid CF (youth)|Real Madrid youth team]], eventually gaining promotion to the main team in 1999, where he became the youngest goalkeeper to play in the [[List of European Cup and UEFA Champions League finals|final of the Champions League]], and to win the title, at 19 years and four days. Casillas became the first choice goalkeeper at Real Madrid, winning two Champions Leagues and La Liga titles in his first three seasons, establishing himself as one of the best goalkeepers in the world. During his highly successful career in Madrid, Casillas won all major club titles, including five [[La Liga]] titles, four [[Supercopa de España]] titles, two [[Copa del Rey]] titles, three [[UEFA Champions League]]s, two [[UEFA Super Cup]]s, two [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cups]] and the [[FIFA Club World Cup]]. After 25 years with Real Madrid, Casillas joined FC Porto in 2015 on a free transfer, where he won the [[2017–18 Primeira Liga|Primeira Liga]] and a [[2018 Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira|Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira]] title. While at Porto, he broke the record for most consecutive seasons played in the UEFA Champions League (20) and amassed the most appearances in the competition (177). He ended his playing career in February 2020, after almost a year on the sidelines following a heart attack he suffered during a training session with Porto in May 2019.

With 167 international caps, Casillas has the second most appearances for the Spain national team, making him the eighteenth-[[List of men's footballers with 100 or more international caps|most capped footballer of all time]]. An unused substitute at [[UEFA Euro 2000]], Casillas became the nation's first choice goalkeeper at the [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002 World Cup]], and went on to play at [[UEFA Euro 2004]] and the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]]. In 2008, he was made [[List of Spain national football captains|captain]], and went on to lead the team to the [[UEFA Euro 2008|European Championship title that year]]. Casillas also led Spain to their first [[2010 FIFA World Cup|World Cup win in 2010]], where he kept a joint–record five clean sheets, winning the [[Yashin Award]] for the best goalkeeper of the tournament. Spain became the first nation to retain the European Championship, winning the title again in [[UEFA Euro 2012|2012]], where he set the record for [[List of UEFA European Championship records and statistics|most consecutive minutes without conceding a goal]] in the competition (509). In 2014, Casillas became one of six players to [[List of players who have appeared in multiple FIFA World Cups|represent Spain at four World Cups]].

In 2008, Casillas placed fourth overall in the [[Ballon d'Or]], and was selected for the [[UEFA Team of the Year]] six consecutive times from 2007 to 2012, a record for a goalkeeper. Casillas was also selected in the [[FIFPro World XI]] a record five times for a goalkeeper, and was named as the [[IFFHS World's Best Goalkeeper]] a record five times, alongside [[Gianluigi Buffon]] and [[Manuel Neuer]]. He was named as the second-best goalkeeper of the 21st century, behind Gigi Buffon, and the second-best goalkeeper of the past 25 years by the same organisation.

==Early life==
Casillas was born on 20 May 1981 in [[Móstoles]], [[province of Madrid]], to José Luis Casillas, a civil servant in the [[Ministry of Education (Spain)|Ministry of Education]], and María del Carmen Fernández González, a hairdresser.<ref name="El Mundo Spain">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.elmundo.es/magazine/m29/textos/iker1.html|title=Iker Casillas, portero del Real Madrid|trans-title=Iker Casillas, Real Madrid's goalkeeper|magazine=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|language=es}}</ref> Both his parents had moved from their home of [[Navalacruz]], [[Province of Ávila|Ávila]].<ref name="El Mundo Spain"/>

Casillas has a brother, seven years younger, named Unai, who used to play as a [[Midfielder#Central midfielder|central midfielder]] for [[CD Móstoles]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://unamadridista.wordpress.com/2010/09/28/get-to-know-unai-casillas/|title=Get to know... Unai Casillas|publisher=Una Madridista|date=28 September 2010|access-date=9 November 2010}}</ref> The brothers' forenames are of [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque]] origin due to a family connection to the region: their paternal grandfather – an officer in the [[Civil Guard (Spain)|Civil Guard]] – was posted to [[Bilbao]] and settled in the city, their father grew up there as a result and Iker also lived in the area as a small child before the family relocated to Madrid.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://ianasagasti.blogs.com/mi_blog/2013/11/casillas-y-el-athletic.html|title=Casillas y el Athletic|trans-title=Casillas and Athletic|publisher=Iñaki Anasagasti Blogs|language=es|date=6 November 2013|access-date=2 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180319004322/https://ianasagasti.blogs.com/mi_blog/2013/11/casillas-y-el-athletic.html|archive-date=19 March 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On one occasion as a young child, when he was seven or eight,<ref name=Lottery/> Casillas forgot to post his father's football predictions for the weekend; his father had correctly predicted all 15 results, and the family lost out on an estimated €1.2&nbsp;million (£1&nbsp;million).<ref>{{cite news|last=McDermott|first=Gerry|title=In off the post: Casillas drops a clanger on lottery|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/in-off-the-post-casillas-drops-a-clanger-on-lottery-25910835.html|access-date=3 April 2018|work=[[Irish Independent]]|date=16 June 2004}}</ref><ref name=Lottery>{{cite news|last=Lowe|first=Sid|title=Casillas eyes win to unite a nation and repay a debt|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/jun/07/euro2004.sport147|access-date=3 April 2018|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=7 June 2004}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Real Madrid===
====Early years====
Casillas began his career in [[Real Madrid CF (youth)|Real Madrid's youth system]], known as [[La Fábrica (Real Madrid)|La Fábrica]], during the 1990–91 season. On 27 November 1997, at age 16 and still a junior, he was first called up to the senior team squad to face [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] in the [[1997–98 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], although he remained on the bench throughout. After spending a season with the [[Real Madrid C|C-team]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://unamadridista.wordpress.com/2011/02/11/iker-casillas-the-real-interview/|title=Iker Casillas – the Real... interview|publisher=Following Real Madrid...|date=11 February 2011|access-date=23 April 2018}}</ref> in the [[Tercera División|fourth tier]], during which they won their regional group,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://arquero-arba.futbolme.net/Nacionales/1998-99/9899-3-7.htm|title=Tercera División (Grupo 7) 1998–99|language=es|publisher=Arquero-Arba|access-date=18 April 2018}}</ref> he came into contention as the club's first-choice between the posts. In starting the [[1999–2000 UEFA Champions League]] group stage fixture against [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiakos]] on 15 September 1999, he became the youngest goalkeeper ever to feature in the competition at the time, aged 18 years and 177 days; a record which was only broken in October 2017 by [[Mile Svilar]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37485398/meet-benfica-mile-svilar-youngest-keeper-champions-league-history|title=Meet Mile Svilar, the youngest keeper in Champions League history|publisher=ESPN FC|last=Yokhin|first=Michael|date=31 October 2017|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref> Three days earlier, Casillas had made his [[La Liga]] debut in a 2–2 draw against [[Athletic Bilbao]] at [[San Mamés Stadium (1913)|San Mamés Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3277/la-liga/2011/09/12/2662477/real-madrids-iker-casillas-making-my-debut-against-athletic|last=Metthews|first=Luke|title=Real Madrid's Iker Casillas: Making my debut against Athletic Bilbao is the greatest memory I have|publisher=Goal|date=12 September 2011|access-date=23 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180423170208/https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3277/la-liga/2011/09/12/2662477/real-madrids-iker-casillas-making-my-debut-against-athletic|archive-date=23 April 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> In May 2000, he became the youngest ever goalkeeper to play in and win a Champions League final when Real Madrid defeated [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] [[2000 UEFA Champions League Final|3–0]], just four days after his 19th birthday.<ref name="Iker Casillas ESPN Profile">{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/players/profile?id=11811&cc=4716|title=Iker Casillas Fernández Profile, Statis, News, Game Log|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|access-date=8 February 2011|archive-date=13 April 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100413085438/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/players/profile?id=11811&cc=4716|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Champions League's greatest ever goalkeepers">{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0e99cb9576d8-81e0528b33a7-1000--champions-league-s-top-goalkeepers-iker-casillas-most-ap/|title=The Champions League's greatest ever goalkeepers|publisher=UEFA|date=20 March 2018|access-date=20 March 2018}}</ref>

====2001–2010====
Casillas lost his place in the side to backup [[César Sánchez]] after poor performances in the [[2001–02 Real Madrid CF season|2001–02 campaign]], but redeemed himself when Sánchez suffered an injury in the final minutes of the [[2002 UEFA Champions League Final|2002 Champions League Final]]. Casillas came on and pulled off several key saves to deny a rampant [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] the Champions League crown. Real Madrid won 2–1.<ref>{{cite news|title=Real crowned champions of Europe|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/champions_league/1984398.stm|work=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=15 May 2002|access-date=31 December 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/competitions/UCL/News/Kind=128/newsId=23850.html|title=Madrid win ninth European crown|publisher=UEFA|date=15 May 2002|access-date=8 April 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020606223553/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/UCL/News/Kind%3D128/newsId%3D23850.html|archive-date=6 June 2002}}</ref>

[[File:Saca Iker Casillas (3869018560).jpg|thumb|255px|right|Casillas in action for Real Madrid at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]] in 2009]]
The [[2007–08 Real Madrid CF season|2007–08 season]] was a fruitful season for Casillas, as he helped Real Madrid reclaim their 31st [[La Liga]] [[List of Spanish football champions|title]] and conceded only 32 goals in 36 matches to claim the [[Zamora Trophy]]. On 14 February 2008, he and club captain [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]] were awarded contracts for life; Casillas signed a contract extension that would keep him at the club until 2017, with an automatic extension if he played 30 competitive matches during the final season of the contract and a buy-out clause of £113&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11827_3146197,00.htm|title=Casillas and Raul commit to Real|publisher=Sky Sports|access-date=7 May 2009|date=14 February 2008}}</ref> His performances earned him a spot in the [[UEFA Team of the Year]] for the second time.

In February 2009, Casillas equalled [[Francisco Buyo|Paco Buyo]]'s record of 454 matches played for a goalkeeper and has since surpassed it to become Real Madrid's most-capped goalkeeper of all time at only 27 years old.<ref>{{cite news|title=Casillas secures place in Madrid folklore|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0d7c89e58ccb-d6cf339f6c89-1000--casillas-secures-a-place-in-madrid-folklore/|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=9 February 2009|access-date=8 February 2011}}</ref> During the 2009 summer transfer window, some Spanish media reported that [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] had launched a record £129&nbsp;million bid for the goalkeeper. The club denied the rumours, however, saying that no such offer had been made. [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] had been rumoured to have enquired about him, but no price was announced.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/city-deny-casillas-bid-975017|title=City deny Casillas bid|date=3 December 2008|access-date=21 February 2026|last=Robson|first=James|work=Manchester Evening News}}</ref> He had been linked with other [[Premier League]] clubs before<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2325833/Iker-Casillas-in-the-dark-over-Tottenham-link.html|title=Iker Casillas in the dark over Tottenham link|date=15 November 2007|access-date=20 October 2010|work=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]|last=Wilson|first=Steve}}</ref> but Casillas himself stated that he "had no intention of leaving" his boyhood club.

During the [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10 season]] on 4 October in a game against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], Casillas made an extraordinary save, running from one side of his goal to the other to deny [[Diego Perotti]] in a one-on-one, close-range encounter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KIceM6T3o-g|title=Real Madrid Vs Sevilla Iker Casillas Huge Save Unbelievable!! HD|via=[[YouTube]]|access-date=28 March 2014}}</ref> After the match, he received praise from fellow Spanish goalkeepers and [[England national football team|England]] goalkeeper [[Gordon Banks]], who stated, "Casillas' reflexes are incredible. If he continues to play this well he will become one of the best goalkeepers in the history of the game." ''[[Europa Press (news agency)|Europa Press]]'' reported that Casillas was the second-most popular Spanish sportsman on the Internet in 2010. The study performed by company Vipnet360 examined the web presence on platforms like Facebook, Twitter and YouTube.<ref>{{cite news|date=27 December 2010|title=Iniesta, Torres, Nadal y Alonso, deportistas españoles más importantes en Internet|trans-title=Iniesta, Torres, Nadal, and Alonso, the most important Spanish athletes on the internet|url=https://www.europapress.es/deportes/futbol-00162/noticia-varios-iniesta-torres-nadal-alonso-nombrados-deportistas-espanoles-mas-importantes-internet-redes-sociales-20101227124812.html|work=[[Europa Press (news agency)|Europa Press]]|language=es}}</ref>

====2010–2015====
[[File:IkerCasillas2010.jpg|thumb|left|Casillas, wearing the captain's armband while playing for Real Madrid in 2010|120px]]
During the [[2010-11 La Liga|2010–11 season]], after the departure of first and second captains of Real Madrid, Raúl and [[Guti (Spanish footballer)|Guti]] respectively, Casillas was selected as first captain with new vice-captains [[Sergio Ramos]], [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]] and [[Gonzalo Higuaín]].

During the [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12 season]], Casillas won the IFFHS Best Goalkeeper award, making him only the second goalkeeper behind [[Gianluigi Buffon]] to win it four times and the only goalkeeper to win the award four times in a row. Casillas played his 600th match for Real Madrid on 22 January 2012 in a 4–1 win against Athletic Bilbao. On 2 May 2012, Casillas clinched his fifth La Liga title and his first as a captain of Real Madrid, with a 3–0 win in Bilbao.

[[File:Iker Casillas's gloves.jpg|thumb|250px|Casillas's gloves on display at the Santiago Bernabeu museum]]
On 22 December 2012, Casillas was dropped by [[José Mourinho]] for a Liga match against [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] in favour of [[Antonio Adán]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/news/liga-mourinho-drops-casillas-malaga-beat-real-madrid-205623479.html|title=Liga – Mourinho drops Casillas as Malaga beat Real Madrid|publisher=Yahoo!|date=22 December 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121225164516/https://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/news/liga-mourinho-drops-casillas-malaga-beat-real-madrid-205623479.html|archive-date=25 December 2012}}</ref> This was the beginning of a series of sour disagreements between the Portuguese coach and the player, some of which, along with other internal affairs, were allegedly aired to the press by Casillas himself. This generated a shift in the opinion of certain sectors of Real Madrid's fans, who gave Casillas the nickname "''topor''" (a [[portmanteau]] of "''topo''", and "''portero''", Spanish for "[[Mole (espionage)|mole]]" and "goalkeeper", respectively).<ref>{{cite web|date=22 May 2013|title=¿Madridismo unido? Los mourinhistas no perdonan a Florentino ni, sobre todo, a Casillas|trans-title=United Madridismo? The Mourinhistas don't forgive Florentino, and especially not Casillas.|url=https://www.vozpopuli.com/deportes/25614-madridismo-unido-los-mourinhistas-no-perdonan-a-florentino-ni-sobre-todo-a-casillas|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130608005943/https://www.vozpopuli.com/deportes/25614-madridismo-unido-los-mourinhistas-no-perdonan-a-florentino-ni-sobre-todo-a-casillas|archive-date=8 June 2013|access-date=27 July 2013|publisher=Voz pópuli}}</ref> During the [[2012–13 La Liga|2012–13 season]], Casillas won the IFFHS Best Goalkeeper Award for the fifth consecutive time, making him the only goalkeeper in history to have ever won that award five times (in a row).

In January 2013, after a serious injury to Casillas, Mourinho signed [[Diego López (footballer, born 3 November 1981)|Diego López]] from Sevilla. López was named first-choice goalkeeper ahead of Adán and kept his place in the team even after Casillas had returned from injury. After the 2012–13 season, Mourinho left Madrid and soon after his departure, Spanish midfielder [[Andrés Iniesta]] criticised him for benching Casillas.

In the middle of 2013, it was announced that [[Carlo Ancelotti]] would be Real Madrid's head coach for the [[2013–14 Real Madrid CF season|2013–14 season]]. Real Madrid started the season with a 2–1 victory over [[Real Betis]] in which Casillas was benched once again. He made his first start in 238 days in the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] group stage match against [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]], but was injured in the 14th minute after Sergio Ramos caught him with an accidental elbow as the goalkeeper came from his line to make a routine catch.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espnfc.com/spanish-primera-divisi%F3n/story/1556396/iker-casillas-injured-after-collision-with-real-madrid-team-mate-sergio-ramos|title=Iker Casillas suffers injury blow|website=Espnfc.com|date=18 September 2013|access-date=26 September 2015}}</ref> Despite being the club's second-choice keeper in [[2013–14 La Liga|La Liga]], behind Diego López, Casillas continued to be Madrid's first choice keeper in the Champions League and [[2013–14 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]], setting a new record of 962 minutes without conceding a goal in the latter competition.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2014/03/01/en/football/real_madrid/1393662091.html|title=Casillas to miss the derby|date=1 March 2014|access-date=27 May 2014|work=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref> In February 2014, he became the first goalkeeper to play in every round of the [[Copa del Rey]] prior to the final without conceding a goal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.kickoff.com/news/41452/iker-casillas-rewrites-spanish-history-books|title=Casillas makes history|date=12 February 2014|access-date=27 May 2014|work=Kickoff|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140527214024/https://www.kickoff.com/news/41452/iker-casillas-rewrites-spanish-history-books|archive-date=27 May 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 16 April, he captained Madrid in [[2014 Copa del Rey Final|the final]] as they beat rivals [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] 2–1 at Valencia's [[Mestalla Stadium]]. On 24 May 2014, Casillas captained Real Madrid in the [[2014 UEFA Champions League Final|2014 Champions League final]], winning the title for the third time in his career with a 4–1 win over [[Atlético Madrid]] in [[Lisbon]]; this was the tenth time Real Madrid had won the trophy. Although [[Diego Godín]]'s opening goal resulted from an error by Casillas, Sergio Ramos tied the match for Real Madrid in injury time; the club went on to win the title in extra-time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c51093bd4a7-41ccc377a75c-1000--madrid-finally-fulfil-decima-dream/|title=Madrid finally fulfil Décima dream|date=24 May 2014|access-date = 9 May 2015|publisher=UEFA|last=Haslam|first=Andrew}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-27563098|title=Champions League: Real Madrid fans celebrate 'La Decima'|date=25 May 2014|access-date=9 May 2015|publisher=BBC|last=Burridge|first=Tom}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/27383593|title=Gareth Bale helped Real Madrid win their 10th European Cup as they finally overwhelmed arch-rivals Atletico Madrid in a compelling Champions League final in Lisbon.|date=24 May 2014|access-date=9 May 2015|website=BBC Sport|last=McNulty|first=Phil}}</ref> In [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|2013–14]] season Casillas kept 6 clean sheets, third most in a single season of Champions League.<ref>{{cite web|title=Champions League's top goalkeepers: Most appearances, clean sheets|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0e99cb9576d8-81e0528b33a7-1000--champions-league-s-top-goalkeepers-most-appearances-clean-s/|website=[[UEFA]]|date=1 January 2023}}</ref>

Following the Champions League win, the [[2014–15 Real Madrid CF season|2014–15 season]] saw Casillas return to being the club's first choice goalkeeper, despite competition from new arrival [[Keylor Navas]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/aug/03/real-madrid-confirm-keylor-navas-signing |title=Real Madrid confirm signing of Costa Rica's goalkeeper Keylor Navas |work=The Guardian |date=3 August 2014 |access-date=11 October 2019 }}</ref> as he then went on to win the [[2014 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]], with Real Madrid defeating Sevilla 2–0 on 12 August 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/news/0250-0c510494bb39-09161ccb7dd2-1000--ronaldo-fires-madrid-to-super-cup-glory/|title = Ronaldo fires Madrid to Super Cup glory|date = 12 August 2014|access-date = 9 May 2015|publisher = UEFA|last = Hart|first = Simon}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.dw.de/kroos-shines-as-real-madrid-win-uefa-super-cup/a-17848608|title = Kroos shines as Real Madrid win UEFA Super Cup|date = 13 August 2014|access-date = 9 May 2015|website = DW Sports|last = Harding|first = Jonathan}}</ref> He then also won the [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]] later that year, making his 700th appearance for Madrid on 20 December 2014, in the [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup Final]], as Real Madrid defeated [[San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] 2–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/12/casillas-won-his-first-club-world-cup-on-his-700th-appearance-with-real-madrid|title=Casillas won his first Club World Cup on his 700th appearance with Real Madrid|last=Navarro|first=Alberto|date=20 December 2014|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|access-date=18 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2014/dec/20/real-madrid-v-san-lorenzo-club-world-cup-live|title = Real Madrid 2–0 San Lorenzo: Club World Cup – as it happened|date = 21 December 2014|access-date = 9 May 2015|website = The Guardian|last = Miller|first = Nick}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.foxsports.com/soccer/story/real-madrid-defeat-san-lorenzo-to-win-fifa-club-world-cup-react-122014|title = Real Madrid claim FIFA Club World Cup title with win over San Lorenzo|date = 20 December 2014|access-date = 9 May 2015|website = FOX Soccer|last = McCarthy|first = Kyle}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://edition.cnn.com/2014/12/20/sport/football/real-madrid-win-club-world-cup/|title = Real Madrid end year with fantastic fourth title in Club World Cup|date = 3 January 2015|access-date = 9 May 2015|publisher = CNN}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://sports.yahoo.com/news/real-madrid-win-club-world-cup-212643137--sow.html|title = Real Madrid win Club World Cup, fourth title of 2014|date = 20 December 2014|access-date = 9 May 2015|website = Yahoo Sports|archive-date = 11 July 2018|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180711042723/https://sports.yahoo.com/news/real-madrid-win-club-world-cup-212643137--sow.html|url-status = dead}}</ref> In May 2015, Casillas played in the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] semi-finals against Juventus, in which his team lost 3–2 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/champions-league/2014-2015/alvaro-morata-haunts-real-madrid-as-juventus-set-up-barca-final_sto4724005/story.shtml|title=Alvaro Morata haunts Real Madrid as Juventus set up Barca final|website=Eurosport|date=13 May 2015 }}</ref>

===Porto===

====2015–2019====
{{Quote box|width=30%|align=Right|quote="You've always been a Real Madrid icon, but above all you've been one of the best representatives of our position on the pitch. Good luck in your new adventure, it'll be strange to see you in another shirt from now on. Go Iker!"|source=—Juventus and Italy goalkeeper [[Gianluigi Buffon]] on Casillas following his transfer to [[FC Porto|Porto]] in July 2015.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/2015/07/13/en/football/real_madrid/1436812635.html|title=Buffon: "Good luck Iker"|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=13 July 2015|access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref>}}
[[File:DK-Porto15 (9).jpg|thumb|right|Casillas playing for Porto in 2015]]
After much speculation about his future, on 11 July 2015 Casillas signed with Portuguese [[Primeira Liga]] side [[FC Porto|Porto]] on a two-year deal with the option of a one-year extension.<ref>{{cite web|title=Official Statement: Iker Casillas|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/07/official-statement-iker-casillas|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|access-date=11 July 2015|date=11 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150712122101/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/07/official-statement-iker-casillas|archive-date=12 July 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-mena/football/premier-league-portuguese/articles/casillas-signs-two-year-porto-contract|title=Casillas signs two-year Porto contract|date=12 July 2015|access-date=21 February 2026|publisher=Bein Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/jul/13/real-madrid-iker-casillas-repair-damage|title=Real Madrid try to repair Iker Casillas damage – but only make things worse|date=14 July 2015|work=The Guardian|access-date=14 July 2015}}</ref> Real Madrid's conduct in his exit was criticised, with Casillas's parents claiming that he was being forced out of the club by president [[Florentino Pérez]], who received calls to quit from fans. Former international teammate [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]], who earlier that summer left Barcelona after a similarly long and successful career, claimed that Real Madrid were ungrateful of Casillas's service to the club.<ref>{{cite news|title=Xavi hits out at Real Madrid for treatment of departing Iker Casillas|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/jul/14/xavi-iker-casillas-real-madrid-porto|access-date=16 August 2015|work=The Guardian|agency=[[Reuters]]|date=14 July 2015}}</ref>

Casillas made his Primeira Liga debut on 15 August, keeping a clean sheet in a 3–0 win over [[Vitória S.C.|Vitória de Guimarães]] at the [[Estádio do Dragão]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Untroubled debut for Iker Casillas|url=https://www.marca.com/en/2015/08/15/en/football/international_football/1439675958.html|access-date=16 August 2015|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=15 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150817214717/https://www.marca.com/en/2015/08/15/en/football/international_football/1439675958.html|archive-date=17 August 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 29 September 2015, he overtook Xavi to become the player with the most appearances in the [[European Cup and UEFA Champions League records and statistics#Appearances|Champions League]], making his record 152nd [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] appearance in a 2–1 home win over [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. That season, Casillas also broke [[Edwin van der Sar]]'s record for the most clean sheets in Champions League history, keeping his 51st clean sheet in the competition on 20 October 2015, in a 2–0 win over [[Maccabi Tel Aviv F.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], as his team climbed top of Champions League Group G.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37439529/iker-casillas-breaks-champions-league-clean-sheet-record|title=Iker Casillas breaks Van der Sar's Champions League clean sheet record|publisher=ESPN FC|date=21 October 2015|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Bennett|first=Edward|title=Most clean sheets in Champions League history: Iker Casillas moves ahead of Chelsea & Man United legends|url=https://www.caughtoffside.com/2015/04/23/most-clean-sheets-in-champions-league-history-iker-casillas-moves-ahead-of-chelsea-man-united-legends/7/|access-date=1 June 2015|date=23 April 2015}}</ref> In January 2016, he was blamed for the away loss at Vitória de Guimarães (1–0) in the [[2015–16 Primeira Liga|league]], following a high-profile error.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/35343302|title=Vitoria Guimaraes 1–0 FC Porto|date=18 January 2016|work=BBC Sport|access-date=20 January 2016}}</ref>

On 11 March 2017, Casillas set a new personal record for clean sheets in a single season with his sixteenth clean sheet in a 4–0 away win over [[F.C. Arouca|Arouca]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2017/03/11/soccer/1489228458_612855.html|title=Iker Casillas breaks own Real Madrid clean sheet record|publisher=AS.com|last=Sanchidrián|first=David F.|date=11 March 2017|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.calciomercato.com/en/news/spanish-goalkeeping-legend-breaks-his-own-record-set-at-real-mad-75686|title=Spanish goalkeeping legend breaks his own record set at Real Madrid|publisher=Calciomercato.com|date=11 March 2017|access-date=15 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316024447/https://www.calciomercato.com/en/news/spanish-goalkeeping-legend-breaks-his-own-record-set-at-real-mad-75686|archive-date=16 March 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 14 March, Casillas made his 175th appearance in UEFA club competitions in a 1–0 away defeat to Juventus in the second leg of the round of 16 of the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], overtaking [[Paolo Maldini]] as the player with the [[UEFA club competition records and statistics#Most appearances in UEFA club competitions|most appearances in European club matches]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/the-biggest-moments-in-iker-casillas-record-setting-uefa-career|title=The biggest moments in Iker Casillas' record-setting UEFA career|work=Fox Sports|last=Dowd|first=Alex|date=14 March 2017|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref>

On 13 September, Casillas equalled [[Ryan Giggs]]'s record of playing in 19 consecutive UEFA Champions League campaigns when he appeared in Porto's 3–1 home defeat to [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] in the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|2017–18 edition of the tournament]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espnfc.com/report?gameId=495317|title=Cenk Tosun stunner leads Besiktas past Porto at the Estadio do Dragao|publisher=ESPN FC|date=13 September 2017|access-date=10 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/2017/09/13/59b997f946163f51288b4603.html|title=Iker Casillas equals Giggs' Champions League record|work=Marca|location=Spain|last1=Lara|first1=Lorenzo|last2=Gillingham|first2=Geoff|date=13 September 2017|access-date=10 October 2017}}</ref> On 2 April 2018, Casillas played his 1,000th match as a professional in Porto's 2–0 loss at [[C.F. Os Belenenses|Belenenses]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Spain legend Iker Casillas makes 1,000th appearances in Porto defeat|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/37549889/spain-legend-iker-casillas-makes-1000th-appearances-porto-defeat|access-date=3 April 2018|publisher=ESPN FC|date=2 April 2018}}</ref> In May, he won his first trophy with the club as they won the league title for the first time since 2013.<ref>{{cite news|title=Porto break Benfica dominance in Portugal to win first league title since 2013 and have a massive party|url=https://talksport.com/football/porto-break-benfica-dominance-portugal-win-first-league-title-2013-and-have-massive-party|access-date=10 May 2018|publisher=Talksport|date=7 May 2018|archive-date=11 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180511082149/https://talksport.com/football/porto-break-benfica-dominance-portugal-win-first-league-title-2013-and-have-massive-party|url-status=dead}}</ref> The [[2017–18 Primeira Liga]] title was confirmed after [[Sporting CP]] and [[Benfica]] tied their respective match.<ref>{{cite web|title=FC Porto crowned champions|url=http://theportugalnews.com/news/fc-porto-crowned-champions/45528|website=The Portugal News Online|publisher=Anglopress Lda|access-date=12 May 2018}}</ref> On 17 May 2018, he renewed his contract with Porto for another year.<ref>{{cite news|title=Casillas to continue with Porto for another year|url=https://en.as.com/en/2018/05/17/football/1526572595_088309.html|work=AS.com|date=17 May 2018|access-date=17 May 2018|archive-date=18 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180518040029/https://en.as.com/en/2018/05/17/football/1526572595_088309.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 4 August, Casillas started in Porto's 3–1 victory over [[C.D. Aves|Desportivo das Aves]] in the [[2018 Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira]].<ref name="2018-Supertaça"/> He surpassed Giggs's record during the 2018–19 season, appearing in his 20th consecutive UEFA Champions League campaign.<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2018/12/13/soccer/1544694127_187030.html|title=Champions League: Iker Casillas still setting European records|publisher=AS|last=Vidal|first=Miguel|date=13 December 2018|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref> On 11 December, Casillas, in a 3–2 away win over Galatasaray, became the first player to reach the knock-out stage 19 times,<ref name=auto/> and become only the second player after Cristiano Ronaldo to win 100 Champions League matches.<ref name=bein/> He made 31 league appearances throughout the season as Porto finished in second place, but his season was cut short after he suffered "an [[acute myocardial infarction]]" during training on 1 May 2019.<ref name="heart attack"/><ref name="coaching-role">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48990814|title=Iker Casillas given coaching role at Porto two months after having heart attack|work=BBC Sport|date=15 July 2019|access-date=25 July 2019}}</ref> He was discharged from hospital on 6 May, but commented that he was uncertain about his future.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48179324|title=Iker Casillas: Porto goalkeeper discharged from hospital after heart attack|work=BBC Sport|date=6 May 2019|access-date=5 November 2019}}</ref>

====2019–2020====
In July 2019, following his heart attack two months earlier, Casillas returned for pre-season training.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48833021|title=Iker Casillas reports for pre-season duty with Porto two months after having a heart attack|publisher=BBC|date=1 July 2019|access-date=2 July 2019}}</ref> Later that month, Porto announced that he had been given a role with the club's coaching staff as he continued his recovery.<ref name="coaching-role"/> In August, he was named in Porto's squad for the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/fc-porto/story/3916464/casillas-named-in-porto-squad-for-new-season|title=Casillas named in Porto squad for new season|work=ESPN FC|date=9 August 2019|access-date=2 September 2019}}</ref> In September, he shared the results of his medical tests on social media;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2019/09/16/football/1568668213_201967.html|title=Iker Casillas shares physical data analytics from Porto training session: "I'm still in the fight..."|website=AS.com|date=16 September 2019|access-date=30 October 2019|archive-date=24 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210224144413/https://en.as.com/en/2019/09/16/football/1568668213_201967.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> at the end of the month, he stated that he would wait until March of the following year to see how he is progressing with his recovery before deciding whether to return to playing or retire. In October, he posted a photo of himself working out in the club's gym on [[Instagram]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2019/10/16/soccer/1571218498_759045.html|title=Iker Casillas delights fans with treadmill workout photograph|website=AS.com|date=16 October 2019|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref> He resumed training on 4 November.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2019/11/04/soccer/1572880992_194193.html|title=Iker Casillas returns to training|website=AS.com|date=4 November 2019|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref>

====Retirement====
On 4 August 2020, Casillas officially announced his retirement from professional football.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/iker-casillas-announces-retirement-from-professional-football-30620784|title=Iker Casillas announces retirement from professional football|website=OneFootball|date=4 August 2020|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref> In July, he was reported to have returned to Real Madrid to work as an advisor for [[Florentino Pérez]].<ref>{{cite web|date=17 July 2020|title=Iker Casillas returns to Real Madrid|last=Caprio|first=Carlos|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/17/5f11cfa646163ffdaa8b4619.html|access-date=21 February 2026|work=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref> In December 2020, he was appointed as the deputy to the Real Madrid Foundation CEO.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/es-ES/noticias/club/comunicados/comunicado-oficial-iker-casillas-04-08-2020|title=Comunicado Oficial: Iker Casillas|website=Real Madrid|language=es|date=22 December 2020|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth career===
Casillas debuted for Spain at the [[Spain national under-17 football team|under-17 level]]. At age 16, he was the youngest player in the Spanish squad that placed third at the [[1997 FIFA U-17 World Championship]] in Egypt. He was later made captain of the U17s. Two years later, he went on to win the [[1999 FIFA World Youth Championship|FIFA World Youth Championship]] and the [[1999 UEFA–CAF Meridian Cup|UEFA–CAF Meridian Cup]] that same year. Initially second-choice, he soon worked his way up to first-choice and eventually earned his first senior cap following some brilliant performances at club level.

===Senior debut, Euro 2000 and 2002 World Cup===
Casillas is currently the second most capped player in the history of the [[Spain men's national football team|Spain national team]]. Following his full international debut at the senior level on 3 June 2000 against [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]] (at 19 years and 14 days),<ref>{{cite news|last=Roldán|first=Isabel|date=7 October 2006|title=Capitán Casillas: todo empezó en Suecia|trans-title=Captain Casillas: it all started in Sweden|url=https://as.com/futbol/2006/10/07/mas_futbol/1160202431_850215.html|access-date=24 May 2024|website=[[Diario AS]]|language=es}}</ref> Casillas was an unused substitute at [[UEFA Euro 2000]]. He was part of the roster for the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]], initially as the understudy to [[Santiago Cañizares]]. Coincidentally, he became first-choice when Cañizares had to withdraw from the tournament due to injury from a freak accident.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport3/worldcup2002/hi/team_pages/spain/newsid_1994000/1994707.stm|title=Canizares out of World Cup|website=BBC Sport|date=17 May 2002|access-date=2 July 2019}}</ref> At 21, Casillas was one of the youngest first-choice goalkeepers in the tournament. He played an instrumental role in Spanish progression when he saved a penalty in regulation time and two more in the 3–2 shoot-out victory during the round of 16 match against the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] (1–1 after 120 minutes), earning him the nickname "The Saint".<ref name="Spain's 2010 conquerors in numbers"/><ref>{{cite news|last=Ingle|first=Sean|title=Ireland 1 – 1 Spain (Spain win 3–2 on pens)|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/jun/16/minutebyminute.worldcupfootball20021|newspaper=The Guardian|date=16 June 2002|access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Sid|last=Lowe|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/jun/17/worldcupfootball2002.sport24|title=Spain breathes sigh of relief|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=17 June 2002|access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref> One of his saves during the quarter-final against co-hosts [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]] during the 2002 World Cup was rated by [[FIFA]] as one of the top ten saves of all time;<ref>FIFA Fever Centennial Anniversary (1904–2004) DVD</ref> however, Spain were eliminated following a 5–3 penalty shoot-out defeat to the Koreans (0–0 after 120 minutes).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport3/worldcup2002/hi/matches_wallchart/spain_v_south_korea/default.stm|title=Korean dream lives on|website=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=BBC|date=22 June 2002|access-date=13 November 2017}}</ref>

===Euro 2004 and 2006 World Cup===
Casillas played in all eight Group six fixtures during [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]] [[UEFA Euro 2004 qualifying|qualifying]], conceding just four goals. He kept a clean sheet in the second leg victory of the playoff against [[Norway national football team|Norway]] which ended 3–0 in [[Oslo]], and started all of Spain's Euro 2004 matches. He was the first choice for the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]], [[Captain (association football)|captaining]] the team twice, but could not prevent ''La Roja'' from losing 3–1 to a [[Zinedine Zidane]]-inspired [[France national football team|France]] in the Round of 16.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4991524.stm|title=Spain 1–3 France|work=BBC Sport|date=27 June 2006|access-date=12 January 2018}}</ref>

===Euro 2008===
With the exclusion of his Real Madrid teammate [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]] from the squad for [[UEFA Euro 2008|Euro 2008]], Casillas was given the captain's armband. He started the first two [[UEFA Euro 2008 Group D|Group D]] games against [[Russia national football team|Russia]] and Sweden before being rested in place of second-choice goalkeeper [[Pepe Reina]] for Spain's group stage elimination of [[Greece national football team|Greece]]. Casillas saved two penalties from [[Antonio Di Natale]] and [[Daniele De Rossi]] as Spain eliminated [[Italy national football team|Italy]] in the quarter-finals with a 4–2 shootout win following a goalless draw on 22 June.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/euro_2008/7468465.stm|title=Spain 0–0 Italy (4–2 pens)|work=BBC News|date=22 June 2008 |access-date=5 January 2010|last=McNulty|first=Phil}}</ref> Spain later went on to win the competition with a 1–0 win over [[Germany national football team|Germany]] in the [[UEFA Euro 2008 Final|final]] on 29 June. Casillas kept clean sheets in all of the quarter-final, semi-final and final matches, with Sweden's first round goal by [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] being the last one scored against him. On 29 June 2008, Casillas became the first goalkeeper-captain to lift the [[UEFA European Championship]] trophy when Spain beat Germany in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=232286&cc=4716&league=UEFA.EURO|title=Germany 0–1 Spain: Torres ends Spain's pain|publisher=[[Soccernet]]|date=29 June 2008|access-date=8 February 2011|archive-date=12 April 2012|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120412013415/https://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=232286&cc=4716&league=UEFA.EURO|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In October 2008, Casillas and back-up Pepe Reina broke the national record for the longest time spent without conceding a goal. The pair went unbeaten for 710 minutes, longer than Spain's longest-serving goalkeeper [[Andoni Zubizarreta]] and Paco Buyo. [[Wesley Sonck]] of [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] ended their goalless streak when he scored against them a [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualifying|2010 World Cup qualifying]] match.

Casillas was the highest-ranked goalkeeper (fourth place) in the [[2008 Ballon d'Or]], behind [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], [[Lionel Messi]] and national teammate [[Fernando Torres]]. Also in 2008, Casillas was named the world's best goalkeeper by the [[International Federation of Football History & Statistics]] (IFFHS).<ref name="Faulhaber">{{cite web|last=Faulhaber|first=Ingo|url=https://www.iffhs.de/?388d85ff8b00388f05f68e05b85fdcdc3bfcdc0aec70aeedb8a212|title=IFFHS|publisher=Iffhs.de|access-date=7 May 2009}}</ref> He also came in third place in the best goalkeepers of all time ranking, beating [[Oliver Kahn]].<ref name="Faulhaber"/>

===2009 Confederations Cup and 2010 World Cup===
[[File:Casillas besando la Copa del Mundo de fútbol.jpg|thumb|Casillas with the [[FIFA World Cup Trophy|World Cup trophy]] during celebrations in Spain, July 2010]]
Casillas was Spain's starting goalkeeper during the [[2009 FIFA Confederations Cup]] in South Africa, making four appearances as Spain finished the tournament in third place. On 5 September 2009, after a 5–0 win over Belgium in a [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group 5#Spain v Belgium|qualifying match for the World Cup]], Casillas equalled Andoni Zubizarreta's national record of 56 clean sheets, and during the team's next match, against [[Estonia national football team|Estonia]] on 9 September 2009, he surpassed Zubizarreta as the record holder for the most Spanish international clean sheets (this being achieved in Casillas's 98th appearance for the national team, while Zubizarreta made 126 before his retirement).<ref>{{cite web|title=PROBABILI FORMAZIONI/Spagna-Francia: ultime novità (qualificazioni mondiali gruppo I)|url=https://www.ilsussidiario.net/News/Calcio-e-altri-Sport/Altre-squadre/2012/10/16/PROBABILI-FORMAZIONI-Spagna-Francia-ultime-novita-qualificazioni-mondiali-gruppo-I-/329556/|access-date=1 June 2015|language=it|date=16 October 2012|archive-date=23 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180823105519/http://www.ilsussidiario.net/News/Calcio-e-altri-Sport/Altre-squadre/2012/10/16/PROBABILI-FORMAZIONI-Spagna-Francia-ultime-novita-qualificazioni-mondiali-gruppo-I-/329556/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Two months later, Casillas made his [[List of men's footballers with 100 or more international caps|100th appearance]] for Spain in its friendly win over [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]], making him only the third player in history of Spanish football to ever reach this far internationally.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=284407&cc=5739&league=FIFA.FRIENDLY|title=Alonso bags brace as Spain underline World Cup credentials|date=14 November 2009|work=ESPN Soccernet|access-date=8 July 2010|archive-date=23 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023080057/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=284407&cc=5739&league=FIFA.FRIENDLY|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Although Casillas committed an error which led to a goal in Spain's 1–0 defeat to Switzerland in their opening match of the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]],<ref name="2010 All-Star Team"/> on 11 July 2010, Casillas captained Spain to their first ever World Cup title with a 1–0 win against the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]] in extra-time.<ref name="Iniesta sinks Dutch with late strike">{{cite news|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=264123&cc=5739&ver=global|title=Iniesta sinks Dutch with late strike|date=11 July 2010|work=[[ESPNsoccernet]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=13 July 2010|archive-date=13 July 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100713192706/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=264123&cc=5739&ver=global|url-status=dead}}</ref> In so doing, he became the third ever goalkeeper to captain a World Cup winning side (along with [[Gianpiero Combi]] in [[1934 FIFA World Cup|1934]] and [[Dino Zoff]] in [[1982 FIFA World Cup|1982]]; the feat was later also achieved by [[Hugo Lloris]] in [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]]). He was voted the tournament's best goalkeeper, being named to the 2010 World Cup Dream Team, and was also awarded the [[Yashin Award|Golden Glove]].<ref name="2010 All-Star Team">{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/newsid=1274177/index.html|title=Spaniards dominate All-Star Team |publisher=FIFA|date=15 July 2010|access-date=15 July 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100718231854/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/newsid%3D1274177/index.html|archive-date=18 July 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Yashin Award"/> In the course of the finals in South Africa, he kept a joint–record five clean sheets – including in all four games in the knock-out stages –,<ref name="2010 All-Star Team"/> only conceded a joint–record two goals, and saved a penalty in regulation time in the quarter-final victory against [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]].<ref name="Spain's 2010 conquerors in numbers"/> In the [[2010 FIFA World Cup Final|final]], he made two crucial stops from Netherlands' [[Arjen Robben]] with the score at 0–0 after the Dutchman had passed all the defenders.<ref name="Iniesta sinks Dutch with late strike"/> Before he went to pick up the [[FIFA World Cup Trophy|World Cup trophy]], Casillas would later state that images of the past captains doing the same was in his head, reeling them off in perfect order going back to the first World Cup he saw as a youngster:

{{blockquote|From when I was small, I saw [[Lothar Matthäus|Matthäus]] lift it. I saw [[Dunga]] lift it, I saw [[Didier Deschamps|Deschamps]] lift it, I saw [[Cafu]] lift it, [[Fabio Cannavaro|Cannavaro]]... so to watch me lift it, I could watch it tomorrow, I could watch it within 10 years and it will always make me emotional because it's incomparable.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/world-cup/world-cup-russia-2018-preview-lionel-messi-ronaldo-italia-90-98-england-brazil-germany-france-a8392211.html|title=A riot of colour, emotion and memories: the World Cup stands alone in the field of sport|work=The Independent|last=Delaney|first=Miguel|date=11 June 2018|access-date=20 August 2018}}</ref>}}

On 15 November 2011, Casillas became Spain's most capped player, breaking Andoni Zubizarreta's record after starting for Spain in their 2–2 draw against [[Costa Rica national football team|Costa Rica]].<ref>{{cite web|first1=Enis|last1=Koylu|title=Real Madrid's Iker Casillas hoping for many more Spain appearances even after equalling all-time record|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/real-madrids-iker-casillas-hoping-132500532.html|publisher=Sports Yahoo|access-date=1 June 2015|date=11 November 2011|archive-date=17 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117030132/https://sports.yahoo.com/news/real-madrids-iker-casillas-hoping-132500532.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 29 February 2012, in Spain's 5–0 win over [[Venezuela national football team|Venezuela]], Casillas equalled Edwin van der Sar's record of 72 international clean sheets. On 30 May, in Spain's 4–1 win over South Korea, Casillas came on for Pepe Reina on the 82nd minute mark. This set the record for most international victories with 95 giving Casillas yet another record to his name. On 6 June, In Spain's 1–0 win over [[China national football team|China PR]], Casillas set the record for most international clean sheets with 74.<ref name="International feats">{{cite web|url=https://m.fifa.com/news/y=2012/m=5/news=international-feats-and-fitting-farewell-1641297.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905093949/https://m.fifa.com/news/y=2012/m=5/news=international-feats-and-fitting-farewell-1641297.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 September 2015|title=International feats and a fitting farewell|publisher=FIFA|access-date=1 June 2015|date=30 May 2012}}</ref>

===Euro 2012===
[[File:Iker Casillas Euro 2012 final trophy.jpg|right|thumb|Casillas lifting the [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]] trophy, the third consecutive major title for [[Spain men's national football team|Spain]], achieving a historic [[Double (association football)#International Double|treble]]]]
Prior to [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]], there had been growing tensions in the dressing room among Spain's players who played for rival clubs Barcelona and Real Madrid; this led manager [[Vicente del Bosque]] to declare that any player who carried this hostility with them at international level would be dropped from the team. As such, Casillas, [[Carles Puyol]], and Xavi called a summit with the manager and the team's players, in order to ease tensions; Casillas was praised in the media for his role in successfully uniting the dressing room.<ref name="head to head"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/spanish-primera-division/15/blog/post/3479536/barcelona-vs-real-madrid-el-clasico-storylines-to-watch|title=Insiders talk Clasico: Camp Nou hoodoo, Messi, Ronaldo, pasillo, more|publisher=ESPN FC|date=4 May 2018|access-date=5 November 2019}}</ref> On 1 July 2012, Casillas became the first player to reach 100 international wins for his country as Spain defeated Italy 4–0 in the [[UEFA Euro 2012 Final|Euro 2012 final]], as Spain successfully defended their title to win their third consecutive major international trophy. He also set another record with his 509 minutes without conceding a goal in that year's [[UEFA Euro 2012|European Championship]], keeping five consecutive clean sheets and breaking the longstanding tally of 494 minutes set by Italian goalkeeper [[Dino Zoff]].<ref name="Casillas, world record-breaking goalkeeper">{{cite web|last=Estepa|first=Javier|title=Casillas, world record-breaking goalkeeper|url=https://www.marca.com/2012/07/02/en/football/national_teams/1341180644.html|work=Marca|location=Spain|access-date=1 June 2015|date=2 July 2012}}</ref> The only goal he conceded, scored by Antonio Di Natale, came in Spain's opening match of the tournament, a 1–1 draw against eventual runners-up Italy.<ref>{{cite web|title=Di Natale: "The goal I scored against Casillas at the 2012 European Championships is the most important. Reaching Roberto Baggio's tally is my goal now|url=http://vivoazzurro.it/en/news/di-natale-il-gol-casillas-alleuropeo-2012-il-piu-prestigioso-ora-voglio-raggiungere-roberto-baggio/|access-date=14 May 2015|date=28 November 2014}}</ref> Casillas then continued his new record unbeaten streak with Spain to 817 minutes, until it was finally broken by [[Olivier Giroud]]'s injury-time goal on 16 October of that year, which came in a 1–1 home draw against France in a [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2014 World Cup qualifying match]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elartedf.com/the-saint/|title=The Saint|publisher=elartedf.com|last=Purty|first=Varun|work=El Arte Del Futbol|date=2 July 2017|access-date=5 November 2019|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191105140044/https://www.elartedf.com/the-saint/}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/international/olivier-giroud-ends-spains-perfect-run-after-hugo-lloris-turns-on-the-heroics-for-france-8214105.html|title=Olivier Giroud ends Spain's perfect run after Hugo Lloris turns on the heroics for France|work=The Independent|last=Jenson|first=Pete|date=17 October 2012|access-date=5 November 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/oct/16/spain-france-world-cup-report|title=France's Olivier Giroud levels in last minute to put Spain in jeopardy|work=The Guardian|last=Lowe|first=Sid|date=16 October 2012|access-date=5 November 2019}}</ref>

===2013 Confederations Cup and 2014 World Cup===
In June 2013, Casillas represented Spain at the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup|2013 Confederations Cup]] in Brazil, making three appearances as Spain reached the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup Final|final]], only to be defeated 3–0 by the [[Brazil national football team|hosts Brazil]] on 30 June, at the [[Maracanã Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Bagchi|first=Rob|date=1 July 2013|work=The Guardian|access-date=21 February 2026|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/jun/30/brazil-spain-live-confederations-cup-final|title=Brazil v Spain: Confederations Cup final – as it happened}}</ref>

In June 2014, Casillas was selected to represent Spain in his fourth [[2014 FIFA World Cup|World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2014/06/12/en/football/national_teams/1402602871.html|title=Casillas: "Winning a second World Cup is in our hands"|date=12 June 2014|access-date=14 June 2014|work=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref> In the team's opening match, he made two mistakes leading to goals from [[Stefan de Vrij]] and [[Robin van Persie]] as the champions were defeated 5–1 by the Netherlands.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-soccer-world-m3-esp-ned-idUSKBN0EO2GF20140613|title=Superb Dutch destroy sorry Spain 5–1|last=Maidment|first=Neil|date=13 June 2014|access-date=21 February 2026|agency=Reuters}}</ref> After the match, Casillas apologised for the defeat and called his performance the worst of his career.<ref>{{cite news|last=Lowe|first=Sid|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jun/14/spain-iker-casillas-worst-performance-holland|title=Spain's Iker Casillas apologises for 'worst performance of my career'|date=14 June 2014|access-date=21 February 2026|work=The Guardian}}</ref> He also started in Spain's second group game against [[Chile national football team|Chile]], which they lost 2–0 and were subsequently eliminated from the World Cup.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gerna|first=Jacopo|title=Brasile 2014, la Spagna chiude un ciclo irripetibile. Come il Barcellona|trans-title=Brazil 2014, Spain ends an un-repeatable cycle. Just like Barcelona|url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Mondiali/18-06-2014/brasile-2014-spagna-chiude-ciclo-irripetibile-come-barcellona-80972204252.shtml|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|access-date=18 May 2015|language=it|date=18 June 2014}}</ref> He received criticism for his role in Chile's second goal, where he punched [[Alexis Sánchez]]'s free kick into the path of the goalscorer [[Charles Aránguiz]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/av/football/27912766|title=World Cup 2014: Iker Casillas mistake gifts Chile's second goal|date=18 June 2014|publisher=BBC|access-date=12 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/88/spain/2015/02/07/8706082/iker-casillas-five-biggest-blunders-from-the-past-year|title=Iker Casillas' five biggest blunders from the past year|date=7 February 2015|website=Goal.com|access-date=31 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150504234009/https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/88/spain/2015/02/07/8706082/iker-casillas-five-biggest-blunders-from-the-past-year|archive-date=4 May 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 23 June, Casillas was left on the bench for Spain's final game against [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]], with Pepe Reina playing instead.

===Euro 2016===
On 5 September 2015, Casillas kept a clean sheet in his 100th game as Spain's captain, a 2–0 [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying|Euro 2016 qualifying]] win over [[Slovakia national football team|Slovakia]] at the [[Estadio Carlos Tartiere]] in [[Oviedo]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/match/spain-vs-slovakia/1653318/report|title=Spain 2–0 Slovakia: Alba and Iniesta put Spain top|publisher=Goal.com|date=5 September 2015|access-date=6 September 2015}}</ref> On 13 November, Casillas kept his 100th international clean sheet with Spain in a 2–0 friendly win over England, in Alicante, becoming the first goalkeeper ever – male or female – to reach this landmark.<ref name="100 clean sheets for Spain">{{cite web|url=https://as.com/diarioas/2015/11/13/english/1447451183_829981.html|title=Casillas into three figures – 100 clean sheets for Spain|publisher=as.com|date=13 November 2015|access-date=20 March 2018|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612142042/https://as.com/diarioas/2015/11/13/english/1447451183_829981.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He equalled the Latvian [[Vitālijs Astafjevs]]'s European record of 166 caps on 27 March 2016 by playing in a friendly against [[Romania national football team|Romania]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0253-0d7f940ce983-3c89370c35f5-1000--casillas-equals-european-caps-record/|title=Casillas equals European caps record|publisher=UEFA|date=27 March 2016|access-date=1 June 2016}}</ref>

On 31 May, Casillas was named to Vicente del Bosque's final 23-man [[UEFA Euro 2016 squads#Spain|Spain squad]] for [[UEFA Euro 2016|Euro 2016]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0253-0d8170a4e457-17a0251aa0fa-1000--isco-and-saul-cut-from-spain-squad/|title=Isco and Saúl cut from Spain squad|publisher=UEFA|first=Daniel|last=Huerta|date=31 May 2016|access-date=1 June 2016}}</ref> The following day, he became the most-capped European player by earning his 167th cap in a 6–1 friendly win over South Korea in [[Salzburg]] in a pre-tournament warm-up match; he was later replaced by debutant [[Sergio Rico]] in the second half. This was his final international appearance.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/4961/international-football/2016/06/01/24156662/casillas-becomes-most-capped-player-in-european-history|title=Casillas becomes most capped player in European history|publisher=Goal.com|last=Judge|first=Matthew|date=1 June 2016|access-date=1 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160613181229/https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/4961/international-football/2016/06/01/24156662/casillas-becomes-most-capped-player-in-european-history|archive-date=13 June 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/444859|title=Spain rout South Korea behind Nolito, Alvaro Morata goals|publisher=ESPN FC|date=1 June 2016|access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref> During the tournament, he was the second-choice goalkeeper behind [[David de Gea]]; Casillas did not make an appearance during the tournament as Spain was eliminated in the Round of 16 following a 2–0 defeat to Italy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37469605/a-history-iker-casillas-vs-gianluigi-buffon-years|title=A history of Iker Casillas vs. Gianluigi Buffon through the years|publisher=ESPN FC|last=Corrigan|first=Dermot|date=14 March 2017|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref>

===2018 World Cup===
On 21 May 2018, Casillas was left out of [[Julen Lopetegui]]'s final 23-man Spain squad for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] in Russia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/world-cup/spain-world-cup-squad-2018-russia-julen-lopetegui-selection-team-alvaro-morata-cesc-fabregas-a8361736.html|title=Spain World Cup squad: Julen Lopetegui's team is as strong as they come and blessed with versatility|work=The Independent|first1=Ed|last1=Malyon|date=21 May 2018|access-date=22 May 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/world-cup/news/2018-world-cup-spain-preview-schedule-tv-and-stream-info-squad-and-players-to-watch/|title=2018 World Cup: Spain preview, schedule, TV and stream info, squad and players to watch|work=CBS Sports|last=Gonzalez|first=Roger|date=22 May 2018|access-date=22 May 2018}}</ref> In November, he hinted a return to the [[Spain men's national football team|Spain football team]] and Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2018/11/16/soccer/1542407030_248646.html|title=Iker Casillas would happily return to Real Madrid and Spain squad|website=AS|date=17 November 2018|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref>

==Style of play and recognition==
[[File:Iker Casillas Euro 2012 final 02.jpg|thumb|right|Casillas making a save in the [[UEFA Euro 2012 final]]]]
{{Blockquote|quote=Honestly, I don't have to use up many words to say how good he is, the results are there for all to see. He has won everything there is to win and has been on the same great level for so many years now, which is possibly hardest of all for a goalkeeper. Spain almost never concede goals and Casillas is the main reason for that.|source=Juventus and Italy goalkeeper [[Gianluigi Buffon]] on Casillas prior to the [[UEFA Euro 2012 Final]].<ref name="head to head">{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0254-0d7e1a168688-03e0c3289645-1000--casillas-and-buffon-go-head-to-head/|title=Casillas and Buffon go head to head|publisher=UEFA|last1=Aikman|first1=Richard|last2=Hunter|first2=Graham|date=30 June 2012|access-date=14 May 2015}}</ref>}}

Widely considered by pundits, as well as both former and current goalkeeping colleagues, as one of the greatest goalkeepers of all time,<ref name="Trendsetters Buffon, Casillas keep it legendary">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37342905/trendsetting-goalkeepers-buffon-casillas-keep-legendary|title=Trendsetters Buffon, Casillas keep it legendary|publisher=ESPN FC|last=Cox|first=Michael|date=25 June 2013|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref><ref name=king>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/2015/07/12/en/football/real_madrid/1436718760.html|title=King of the keepers|work=Marca|location=Spain|author1=J. L. HURTADO|author2=H. CEREZO|date=7 December 2015|access-date=14 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171026110831/https://www.marca.com/en/2015/07/12/en/football/real_madrid/1436718760.html|archive-date=26 October 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://football-italia.net/buffon-casillas-the-best/|title=Buffon: 'Casillas the best'|publisher=Football Italia|date=19 November 2015|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/sports/soccer/blog/_/name/schaerlaeckens_leander/id/6067671/manchester-united-edwin-van-der-sar-ranks-all-greats|title=Van der Sar ranks among the all-time greats|publisher=ESPN|date=28 January 2011|access-date=2 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/2015/05/04/en/football/real_madrid/1430759936.html|title=Zoff: "Buffon or Casillas? I prefer Casillas"|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=5 April 2015|access-date=2 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107002600/https://www.marca.com/en/2015/05/04/en/football/real_madrid/1430759936.html|archive-date=7 November 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> Casillas was given the nickname "''San Iker''" ("Saint Iker") throughout his career, for his precocious performances as a youngster, and due to his ability to produce acrobatic and decisive saves. In his prime, he was a spectacular, well-rounded, and athletic keeper, who was known in particular for his outstanding agility, reflexes, consistency and shot-stopping, as well as his foot-work, positioning between the posts, concentration, and speed when [[Goalkeeper (association football)#Sweeper-keeper|rushing off his line]] in one on one situations;<ref name="Iker Casillas ESPN Profile"/><ref name=king/><ref name="club">{{cite web|date=28 March 2007|title=Casillas nel club dei numero uno|trans-title=Casillas in the number one club|url=https://it.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0254-0d7ba3d555ea-88cffc361ccf-1000--casillas-nel-club-dei-numero-uno/|access-date=14 March 2017|publisher=UEFA|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Vocalelli|first=Alessandro|date=30 June 2012|title=Da Buffon-Casillas a Balotelli-Torres Italia contro Spagna ruolo per ruolo|trans-title=From Buffon-Casillas to Balotelli-Torres: Italy against Spain, role by role.|url=https://www.repubblica.it/speciali/calcio/europei/polonia-ucraina2012/squadre/italia/2012/06/30/news/italia_spagna_ruolo_per_ruolo-38269386/|access-date=14 March 2017|work=[[La Repubblica]]|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/spain/9367049/Euro-2012-I-look-up-to-Italy-goalkeeper-Gianluigi-Buffon-reveals-Spains-No-1-Iker-Casillas.html|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/spain/9367049/Euro-2012-I-look-up-to-Italy-goalkeeper-Gianluigi-Buffon-reveals-Spains-No-1-Iker-Casillas.html|archive-date=11 January 2022|url-access=subscription|url-status=live|title=Euro 2012: I look up to Italy goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon, reveals Spain's No 1 Iker Casillas|work=The Telegraph|last=Winter|first=Henry|date=30 June 2012|access-date=14 March 2017}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref name=salute>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0254-0d7ba062f478-005daacaf6fa-1000--spanish-legends-salute-casillas/|title=Spanish legends salute Casillas|publisher=UEFA|last=Brown|first=Lucas|date=28 March 2007|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/kiko-casilla-for-a-goalkeeper-messi-and-cristiano-are-the-opponents-to-beat|title=Kiko Casilla: "For a goalkeeper, Messi and Cristiano are the opponents to beat"|publisher=La Liga|date=2 January 2015|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref><ref name="Left-Footed World XI">{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1247190-picking-an-all-time-left-footed-world-football-xi|title=The All-Time, Left-Footed World Football XI|publisher=Bleacher Report|last=Matchett|first=Karl|date=4 July 2012|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref> he has also stood out for his penalty-saving abilities.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/2015/10/05/en/football/international_football/1444072758.html|title=The game's top penalty-stoppers|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=10 May 2015|access-date=14 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171026111459/https://www.marca.com/en/2015/10/05/en/football/international_football/1444072758.html|archive-date=26 October 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/news/y=2012/m=2/news=meet-the-penalty-killers-1585700.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924184651/http://www.fifa.com/news/y=2012/m=2/news=meet-the-penalty-killers-1585700.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=24 September 2015|title=Meet the penalty killers|publisher=FIFA|date=17 February 2012|access-date=14 March 2017}}</ref> 

In spite of his reserved character, he has been highly regarded for his strong personality, calm composure under pressure, ability to organise his defence, and leadership from the back throughout his career, as well as his reading of the game.<ref name="Iker Casillas ESPN Profile"/><ref name=salute/><ref name="Left-Footed World XI"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/soccer/casillas-iker-final/|title=Spain victory lies in the hands of Casillas|publisher=Sportsnet.ca|date=15 September 2009|access-date=27 March 2017}}</ref><ref name="Casillas vs. Buffon">{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11946/9846537/iker-casillas-versus-gianluigi-buffon-which-one-is-the-better-goalkeeper|title=Iker Casillas versus Gianluigi Buffon: Which one is the better goalkeeper?|publisher=Sky Sports|last=Bate|first=Adam|date=13 May 2015|access-date=27 March 2017}}</ref> Gianluigi Buffon described Casillas as the best goalkeeper of his era with his hands.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.90min.com/posts/2732836-gianluigi-buffon-names-arsenal-s-petr-cech-as-the-best-goalkeeper-of-his-era|title=Gianluigi Buffon Names Arsenal's Petr Cech as the Best Goalkeeper of his Era|publisher=90min|first=Mahmoud|last=Jaber|date=18 November 2015|access-date=8 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/spain-group-a-1.841307|title=SPAIN – GROUP A|publisher=Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|date=1 June 2009|access-date=17 May 2020}}</ref> He was also known for his ability to save the ball with his feet, with former goalkeeper [[Manuel Almunia]] likening him to compatriot [[Luis Arconada]], who also served as an inspiration to Casillas, and to whom he was often compared throughout his career, due to his quick reactions, movement, and excellent footwork. Regarding Casillas's playing style and goalkeeping ability, Almunia commented in 2017: "Iker's a strong goalkeeper, leaps well, good diving in either direction... between the posts he moves like a cat."<ref name=salute/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2017/12/13/soccer/1513169565_572541.html|title=Manuel Almunia: "Kepa is good with his feet, like Luis Arconada"|publisher=AS.com|last=Ruiz|first=Marco|date=13 December 2017|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0d800ac7fedf-e79ccb7322bd-1000--casillas-carrying-the-torch-for-his-fellow-keepers/|title=Casillas carrying the torch for his fellow keepers|publisher=UEFA|first=Alfredo|last=Rodríguez|date=24 March 2015|access-date=27 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.org/news/newsid=949435.html|title=Casillas names his top ten No1s|publisher=UEFA|last=Balagué|first=Guillem|date=5 February 2010|access-date=27 March 2017|archive-date=28 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170328195704/https://www.uefa.org/news/newsid=949435.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2016, Casillas was named the  fourth greatest goalkeeper in history by [[France Football]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://football-italia.net/buffon-voted-greatest-keeper/|title=Buffon voted greatest 'keeper|publisher=Football Italia|date=12 February 2016|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref>

A precocious talent in his youth, Casillas has drawn praise for his longevity and consistency at the top level,<ref name="Trendsetters Buffon, Casillas keep it legendary"/><ref name=king/><ref name=club/><ref name=salute/> as well as his discipline in training;<ref name="head to head"/> despite his reputation and goalkeeping ability, however, due to his lack of notable height and strong physical attributes, he has been criticised at times by pundits for struggling to command his area, in particular against aerial threats, and for his unsteady handling and indecisiveness when coming out to claim crosses, as he often preferred to punch the ball away. He also received criticism in the media for a series of errors and less consistent performances in his later career, as he lost some of his speed and mobility with age due to his physical decline.<ref name="Iker Casillas ESPN Profile"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2013/09/16/en/football/real_madrid/1379348389.html|title=Casillas to face bombardment|work=Marca|location=Spain|last=Cerezo|first=Hugo|date=16 September 2013|access-date=17 November 2016}}</ref><ref name="Casillas is not commanding at crosses or good with his feet">{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/2014/12/23/en/football/real_madrid/1419339112.html|title=Casillas is not commanding at crosses or good with his feet|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=23 December 2014|access-date=17 November 2016|archive-date=18 November
