2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161118162953/https://www.marca.com/en/2014/12/23/en/football/real_madrid/1419339112.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.repubblica.it/speciali/mondiali/brasile2014/spagna/2014/06/14/news/il_declino_di_san_iker_simbolo_di_una_squadra_che_non_c_pi-88923979/|title=l declino di San Iker, simbolo di una squadra che non-c'è più|publisher=La Repubblica|language=it|last=Sorrentino|first=Andrea|date=14 June 2014|access-date=14 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2627455-5-reasons-why-gianluigi-donnarumma-needs-to-continue-his-career-at-ac-milan#slide0|title=5 Reasons Why Gianluigi Donnarumma Needs to Continue His Career at AC Milan|work=Bleacher Report|last=Lopresti|first=Sam|date=25 March 2016|access-date=8 October 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/soccer/a-closer-look-at-spains-euro-2012-squad/article4235828/|title=A closer look at Spain's Euro 2012 squad|work=[[The Globe and Mail]]|date=6 June 2012|access-date=17 May 2020}}</ref> Although he has occasionally been criticised by pundits for his limited skills with the ball at his feet in comparison to other Spanish goalkeepers, Casillas's distribution with both his hands and feet has generally been reliable throughout his career, and he is capable of sending the ball into deep areas of the pitch with his long throws and kicks with his left foot.<ref name="Trendsetters Buffon, Casillas keep it legendary"/><ref name="Left-Footed World XI"/><ref name="Casillas is not commanding at crosses or good with his feet"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2012/11/25/en/football/real_madrid/1353873213.html|title=Casillas has problems with his footwork|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=25 November 2012|access-date=25 May 2017}}</ref>

==Sponsorship==
In January 2012, Casillas agreed a sponsorship deal with [[Adidas]] to wear their Response goalkeeping gloves and Predator football boots.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.footballboots.co.uk/4655-adidas-sign-iker-casillas-from-reebok.html|title=Adidas sign Iker Casillas from Reebok|publisher=FootballBoots.co.uk|access-date=16 January 2012|archive-date=23 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323003507/https://www.footballboots.co.uk/4655-adidas-sign-iker-casillas-from-reebok.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> The move to Adidas ended a long running association for Casillas with [[Reebok]], which started in 2004. In February 2005, Casillas was the football face of Reebok's "I Am What I Am" global integrated advertising campaign that linked all the brand's marketing efforts under one umbrella.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://corporate.reebok.com/en/about_reebok/faq_section/marketing/default.asp|title=Reebok Marketing|publisher= corporate.reebok.com|access-date=16 January 2012|archive-date=25 December 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071225164638/https://corporate.reebok.com/en/about_reebok/faq_section/marketing/default.asp|url-status=dead}}</ref> Adidas has been the parent company of Reebok since 2005.

==Outside football==
===Personal life===
[[File:14-6-2011 Visita Iker Casillas (5833110137) (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|alt=A man smiling. He has a short hair.|Casillas in 2011]]
Between 2004 and 2008, Casillas dated beauty pageant winner [[Eva González]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-11-30 |title=Eva González: su carácter acaba con sus relaciones|url=https://e00-elmundo.uecdn.es/loc/2013/11/30/529895b761fd3d8f578b4580.html|access-date=28 June 2025|work=El Mundo|language=es}}</ref> Casillas was in a relationship with sports journalist [[Sara Carbonero]] from 2009 to 2021.<ref name=":0">{{cite news|last=Tiramillas|first=Redacción|date=12 March 2021|title=Iker Casillas y Sara Carbonero confirman su separación: "Es una decisión de mutuo acuerdo"|url=https://www.marca.com/tiramillas/2021/03/12/604bcd64268e3e9f048b4612.html|access-date=28 June 2025|work=Marca|language=es}}</ref> Their first son Martín was born on 3 January 2014 in [[Madrid]].<ref>{{cite news|date=3 January 2014|title=That's my boy! Iker Casillas' son is born - MARCA.com (English version)|url=https://www.marca.com/2014/01/03/en/football/real_madrid/1388772056.html|access-date=21 February 2026|work=Marca}}</ref> In November 2015, the couple announced they were expecting their second child. On 20 March 2016, the couple married. On June 2, 2016, their second son Lucas was born.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sara Carbonero on Real Madrid legend Iker Casillas: I'm lucky to share my life with him|url=https://www.tribalfootball.com/articles/sara-carbonero-on-real-madrid-legend-iker-casillas-i-m-lucky-to-share-my-life-with-him-4087403|access-date=28 June 2025|website=www.tribalfootball.com}}</ref> On 1 May 2019, during Porto's morning training session, Casillas was rushed to hospital after suffering a [[myocardial infarction|heart attack]] at the club's training ground, where his situation was stabilized.<ref name="heart attack">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48125061|title=Iker Casillas: Porto goalkeeper taken to hospital following heart problems|date=1 May 2019|work=BBC News|access-date=1 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=1 May 2019|title=Information on the clinical condition of Iker Casillas|url=https://www.fcporto.pt/en/news/20190501-en-information-on-the-clinical-condition-of-iker-casillas|access-date=28 June 2025|website=fcporto.pt}}</ref> Later that evening, Casillas, whose situation had improved, published a statement on [[Twitter]] with a picture of himself giving the [[Thumb signal|thumbs up signal]] in which he thanked the people for the moral support they gave him.<ref>{{cite tweet|number=1123664609641103360|title=Todo controlado por aquí, un susto grande pero con las fuerzas intactas. Muchísimas gracias a todos por los mensajes y el cariño|user=IkerCasillas|language=Spanish|date=1 May 2019|access-date=1 May 2019}}</ref> Later that month, it was announced that his wife was suffering from [[cancer]].<ref>{{cite news|date=22 May 2019|title=Iker Casillas: Wife battling cancer weeks after keeper's heart attack|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48362541|access-date=28 June 2025|work=BBC Sport|language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 12 March 2021, Casillas and Carbonero announced their decision to separate.<ref name=":0"/> In 2013, a street in the [[Móstoles]] municipality of Madrid was renamed ''Avenida de Iker Casillas'' in his honour.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ein Madridista sagt Adios Real: Der Weg des "San Iker"|url=https://www.kicker.de/ein-madridista-sagt-adios-real_der-weg-des-san-iker-596070/slideshow|access-date=28 June 2025|website=kicker|language=de-DE}}</ref> On 17 February 2020, Casillas confirmed his intention to stand as a candidate in the [[RFEF]] presidential elections.

===Charity===
In 2011, Casillas was appointed as a Goodwill Ambassador for the [[United Nations Development Programme]]'s [[Millennium Development Goals]].<ref>[http://content.undp.org/go/newsroom/2011/january/le-footballer-iker-casillas--nouvel-ambassadeur-de-bonne-volont--des-nations-unies.en Iker Casillas appointed new UNDP Goodwill Ambassador] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110414152718/http://content.undp.org/go/newsroom/2011/january/le-footballer-iker-casillas--nouvel-ambassadeur-de-bonne-volont--des-nations-unies.en|date=14 April 2011}}. Content.undp.org. 24 January 2011. Retrieved 17 March 2012.</ref><ref>[https://www.un.org/apps/news/story.asp?NewsID=37365&Cr=undp&Cr1= Spain's goalkeeper Casillas to score poverty reduction goals as UN Goodwill Ambassador]. Un.org. 24 January 2011. Retrieved 17 March 2012.</ref>

He has his own charitable foundation, the ''Fundación Iker Casillas''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ikercasillasworld.com/es/fundacion/fundacion-iker-casillas/|title=Objetivos de la Fundación Iker Casillas|publisher=ikercasillasworld.com|language=es|last1=Iker Casillas Foundation|access-date=29 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171001190651/http://www.ikercasillasworld.com/es/fundacion/fundacion-iker-casillas/|archive-date=1 October 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2018, he attended the international social [[Football for Friendship]] forum in Moscow.<ref>{{cite web|title=2018 FIFA World Cup - News - 211 countries and regions take part in the Sixth International Football for Friendship Children's Forum|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/211-countries-and-regions-took-part-in-the-sixth-international-football-for-frie|access-date=14 November 2020|website=www.fifa.com|language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Records'''
*[[List of footballers with 100 or more UEFA Champions League appearances|Second-most appearances in the UEFA Champions League]]: 177 (behind [[Cristiano Ronaldo]]) (excluding 4 appearances in the qualifying rounds)<ref name="auto" />
*[[European Cup and UEFA Champions League records and statistics#Goalkeeping|Second-most clean sheets in the UEFA Champions League]]: 57 (excluding 2 in the qualifying rounds) (behind [[Manuel Neuer]])<ref name="Champions League's greatest ever goalkeepers"/>
*[[European Cup and UEFA Champions League records and statistics#Most wins|Third-most victories in the UEFA Champions League]]: 101 (behind [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] and [[Thomas Müller]])<ref name=bein>{{cite web|url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/uefa-champions-league/articles/casillas-reaches-100-champions-league-wins-2|title=Casillas reaches 100 Champions League wins|website=beinSports|date=11 December 2018|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref>
*Most consecutive seasons in the UEFA Champions League: 20<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/newsid=2564139.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180918093727/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/newsid=2564139.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 September 2018|title=Record 20th Champions League campaign for Casillas|publisher=UEFA|date=18 September 2018|access-date=14 December 2018}}</ref>
*First player in UEFA Champions League history to reach the knockout phase 19 times<ref name="auto" />
*First goalkeeper to win 100 UEFA Champions League matches<ref name=bein/>
*Youngest goalkeeper to play in a UEFA Champions League final: 19 years and 4 days<ref name="Iker Casillas ESPN Profile"/><ref name="Champions League's greatest ever goalkeepers"/>
*Youngest goalkeeper to win a UEFA Champions League final: 19 years and 4 days<ref name="Iker Casillas ESPN Profile"/><ref name="Champions League's greatest ever goalkeepers"/>
*Second-most UEFA Champions League titles won by a goalkeeper: 3 (behind [[Juan Alonso (footballer, born 1927)|Juan Alonso]]) (alongside [[Ray Clemence]], [[Sepp Maier]], [[Keylor Navas]], [[Heinz Stuy]], [[Víctor Valdés]] and [[Kiko Casilla]])<ref name="Champions League's greatest ever goalkeepers"/>
*Most appearances for Real Madrid in UEFA club competitions: 155<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/teams/50051--real-madrid/|title=Real Madrid CF|publisher=UEFA|access-date=20 March 2018}}</ref>
*Most [[IFFHS World's Best Goalkeeper]] Awards: 5 (alongside Gianluigi Buffon and [[Manuel Neuer]])<ref name="Former Results"/>
*Most appearances by a goalkeeper in the [[FIFPRO#FIFA FIFPRO World 11|FIFPro World XI]]: 5
*Most appearances by a goalkeeper in the [[UEFA Team of the Year]]: 6<ref name="UUTOTY"/>
*Second-most appearances for the Spain national team: 167 (behind [[Sergio Ramos]])<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eu-football.info/_players.php?id=185 |title = Statistics&nbsp;– Most-capped players|website=EU-Football.info|access-date =9 January 2016}}</ref><ref name="Most caps">{{cite web|url=https://www.bdfutbol.com/en/c/rankingPSEL.html|title=Ranking&nbsp;– Played Matches|website=BDFutbol|access-date=28 December 2015}}</ref>
*Most international clean sheets: 102<ref name="International feats"/><ref name="100 clean sheets for Spain"/>
*Third-most international victories: 121<ref name="International feats"/><ref name="Most caps"/> (behind [[Sergio Ramos]] and [[Cristiano Ronaldo]])<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/06/07/5cfa4f1746163f39098b45a0.html|last=Lara|first=Miguel Ángel|title=Sergio Ramos set to break world record|website=Marca|location=Spain|date=7 June 2019|access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref>
*[[List of players who have appeared in the most FIFA World Cups#Tournaments|Most FIFA World Cup tournaments played for Spain]]: 4 (alongside Xavi, Andoni Zubizarreta, Fernando Hierro, Andrés Iniesta, Sergio Ramos and Sergio Busquets)
*[[List of UEFA European Championship records and statistics#Goalkeeping|Longest unbeaten run at the UEFA European Championship]]: 509 minutes<ref name="Casillas, world record-breaking goalkeeper"/>
*Most clean sheets at the UEFA European Championship: 9 (alongside [[Edwin van der Sar]])
*Most clean sheets in a single edition of UEFA European Championship: 5 (in [[UEFA Euro 2012|2012]], alongside [[Jordan Pickford]] in [[UEFA Euro 2020|2020]])
*Fewest goals conceded in a single edition of the UEFA European Championship: 1 (in 2012, alongside Gianluigi Buffon, [[Thomas Myhre]], and Dino Zoff)
*[[List of UEFA European Championship records and statistics#Penalty shoot-outs|Most penalty kicks saved in penalty shoot-outs at the UEFA European Championship]]: 3 (alongside Gianluigi Buffon)
*Only goalkeeper to stop penalties in two different editions of the FIFA World Cup (excluding shoot-outs): 2002 (vs Ireland), 2010 (vs Paraguay)<ref name="Spain's 2010 conquerors in numbers">{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/spain-s-2010-conquerors-in-numbers-2904843|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180607103350/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/spain-s-2010-conquerors-in-numbers-2904843|url-status=dead|archive-date=7 June 2018|title=Spain's 2010 conquerors in numbers|publisher=FIFA|date=22 August 2017|access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref>
